notes: SEQN is the unique participant identifier in NHANES. It maps to person_source_value to retain the original identifier, while person_id is an internally generated OMOP identifier.

Dietary day one sample weight is a survey design weight. It can be stored in the observation table with a custom concept for the observation_concept_id (e.g., a local concept for 'Dietary day one sample weight') and the numeric value in value_as_number.
Dietary two-day sample weight is a survey design weight. Similar to WTDRD1, it is stored as a numeric observation with a custom concept_id.

Dietary recall status is a categorical variable indicating the quality/completeness of the recall. It maps to value_as_concept_id in the observation table, using a local/custom concept for the status categories.
Interviewer ID code is an identifier for the interviewer. It can be stored as a string in the observation table, as there is no standard OMOP table for interviewer identifiers.
Breast-fed infant status is a binary variable. It can be mapped to a standard concept (e.g., SNOMED 'Breast fed') or a local concept, stored in value_as_concept_id.
Number of days of intake is an ordinal count. It can be stored as a numeric value in the observation table with a custom concept for the observation_concept_id.
Number of days between intake and household interview is a continuous numeric variable. It maps to value_as_number in the observation table.
Intake day of the week is a categorical variable. It can be mapped to standard concepts for days of the week (e.g., SNOMED) or local concepts, stored in value_as_concept_id.
Language used mostly is a categorical variable. It can be mapped to standard language concepts (e.g., ISO 639-3 in OMOP Vocabulary) or local concepts, stored in value_as_concept_id.
Main respondent indicator is categorical (e.g., self, proxy). It can be mapped to custom concepts for respondent type and stored in value_as_concept_id.
Helped in responding indicator is categorical. It can be mapped to custom concepts (e.g., Yes/No/Not applicable) and stored in value_as_concept_id.
Number of foods/beverages reported is a continuous count. It maps to value_as_number in the observation table.
Salt used at table yesterday is a binary variable. It can be mapped to standard Yes/No concepts (e.g., SNOMED) or local concepts, stored in value_as_concept_id.
Type of salt used is categorical (e.g., ordinary, sea salt, lite salt). It can be mapped to standard concepts for salt types or local concepts, stored in value_as_concept_id.
